name: Total area of land developed for rice cultivation (Ha)
definition: The total area of land developed for rice cultivation by project beneficiaries during the reporting period. The area includes both newly developed and existing rice fields planted during the reporting period. Each cultivated plot is counted once regardless of the number of cropping cycles.
numerator: Total area, in hectares, of land developed for rice cultivation under project support during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Add together the hectares of land developed for rice cultivation across all sites during the reporting period. Each plot is counted once, even if it was cultivated multiple times within the period.
formula: Sum the hectares of land developed for rice by project beneficiaries across all sites during the reporting period.
data_source: Farmer production records, GPS measurements, household surveys, extension records, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected through farmer surveys, extension officer records, GPS field measurements, and field verification visits using standardized data collection tools.
means_of_verification: Farmer registers, GPS measurements, household survey reports, field inspection reports, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Land under rice cultivation is accurately measured and reported using standardized measurement methods.
limitations: Measurement errors or inaccurate reporting of cultivated land area may affect the accuracy of the reported results.

name: Total beneficiaries of the land developed for rice cultivation (#)
definition: The total number of individuals who directly benefit from the areas developed for rice cultivation during the reporting period. Each beneficiary is counted once, regardless of how many times or in how many ways they benefit.
numerator: Total number of individuals directly benefiting from the areas developed for rice cultivation during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Sum the number of individuals directly benefiting from the land developed for rice cultivation across all sites during the reporting period. Each beneficiary is counted once.
formula: Sum the number of direct beneficiaries of the land developed for rice cultivation across all sites during the reporting period.
data_source: Beneficiary registers, cooperative membership records, and project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected through beneficiary registration forms, and project monitoring database.
means_of_verification: Beneficiary registers, farmer association records, and field verification reports.
assumptions: All beneficiaries are accurately identified and recorded
limitations: Incomplete beneficiary information may result in inaccurate beneficiary counts.

Each parcel of land is counted once after the allocation has been officially approved and documented.

name: Percentage increase in rice crop yield (%)
definition: The percentage increase in the average rice yield of project beneficiaries compared with the baseline, measured in metric tons per hectare (MT/ha).
numerator: Difference between the average rice yield during the reporting period and the baseline average rice yield (MT/ha).
calculation_method: Calculate the average rice yield (MT/ha) for project beneficiaries during the reporting period, compare it with the baseline yield, and express the change as a percentage.
formula: [(Average yield at reporting period − Average baseline yield) ÷ Average baseline yield] × 100
data_source: Crop-cutting surveys, farmer records, household surveys, project monitoring data, and agricultural production reports.
collection_method: Yield data are collected through crop-cutting surveys, farmer records, and household surveys, and verified by extension officers.
means_of_verification: Crop-cutting reports, farmer records, household survey data, project monitoring reports, and agricultural statistics.
responsible: M&E Manager, Agricultural Specialist, and Project Data Analyst.
assumptions: Farmers adopt project-supported technologies, favourable weather conditions prevail, and accurate production records are maintained.
limitations: Rice yield may be affected by weather, pests, diseases, and other external factors beyond the project's control.

name: Percentage increase in rice production (%)
definition: The percentage increase in the total quantity of rice produced by project beneficiaries compared with the baseline, measured in metric tons (MT).
numerator: Difference between total rice production during the reporting period and total baseline rice production (MT).
calculation_method: Calculate the total rice production by project beneficiaries during the reporting period, compare it with the baseline production, and express the change as a percentage.
formula: [(Total rice production during the reporting period − Total baseline rice production) ÷ Total baseline rice production] × 100
data_source: Household surveys, farmer records, crop-cutting surveys, project monitoring reports, and agricultural production statistics.
collection_method: Production data are collected through household surveys, crop-cutting surveys, and farmer records, and verified through field monitoring.
means_of_verification: Crop-cutting reports, farmer records, household survey data, project monitoring reports, and agricultural statistics.
responsible: M&E Manager, Agricultural Specialist, and Project Data Analyst.
assumptions: Farmers adopt project-supported technologies, favourable weather conditions prevail, and accurate production records are maintained.
limitations: Rice yield may be affected by weather, pests, diseases, and other external factors beyond the project's control.

name: Percentage increase in beneficiaries' income from rice production (%)
definition: The percentage increase in the average annual net income earned by project beneficiaries from rice production during the reporting period compared with the baseline. Net income is calculated as revenue from rice sales minus direct production costs.
numerator: Difference between the average annual net income from rice production and the baseline average annual net income.
calculation_method: Calculate the average annual net income from rice production, compare it with the baseline, and express the change as a percentage.
formula: [(Average annual net income during the reporting period − Average annual baseline net income) ÷ Average annual baseline net income] × 100
data_source: Household surveys, farmer records, project monitoring data, and beneficiary interviews.
collection_method: Income data are collected through household surveys, and farm records.
means_of_verification: Crop-cutting reports, farmer records, household survey data, project monitoring reports, and agricultural statistics.
responsible: M&E Manager, Agricultural Specialist, and Project Data Analyst.
assumptions: Beneficiaries maintain accurate production and sales records, reliable production costs and revenues.
limitations: Income may be affected by external factors, and self-reported income data may be subject to recall bias.

name: Percentage increase in the area cultivated by the private sector under rice value chain (%)
definition: The percentage increase in the total area cultivated by private sector actors under the rice value chain compared with the baseline.
numerator: Difference between the average annual net income from rice production and the baseline average annual net income.
denominator: Total baseline area cultivated by private sector actors (ha).
calculation_method: Calculate the total area cultivated by private sector actors, compare it with the baseline, and express the change as a percentage.
formula: [(Area cultivated during the reporting period − Baseline cultivated area) ÷ Baseline cultivated area] × 100
data_source: Farm records, GPS field measurements, project monitoring data, household surveys, and extension reports.
collection_method: Data are collected through farm surveys, GPS field measurements, and production records, and verified through field inspections.
means_of_verification: Household survey data, GPS measurements, farm records, extension reports, and project monitoring reports.
responsible: M&E Manager, Agricultural Specialist, and Project Data Analyst.
assumptions: Private sector actors continue investing in rice production and maintain reliable farm records.
limitations: Cultivated area may be influenced by external factors such as weather, land availability, and government policies beyond the project's control.

means_of_verification: Household survey reports, beneficiary databases, project monitoring reports, and evaluation reports.
assumptions: Beneficiaries accurately report income, project interventions increase earnings, and reliable baseline and follow-up income data are available.
limitations: Income may be affected by external factors such as market prices, weather, and government policies, while self-reported income may be subject to recall bias.

name: Total number of jobs created (#)
definition: The total number of new jobs created as a direct result of project-supported interventions during the reporting period. This includes full-time, part-time, seasonal, and self-employment opportunities. Each individual is counted once during the reporting period.
numerator: Number of individuals with new jobs.
calculation_method: Count the total number of female project beneficiaries whose annual income increased above the baseline as a result of project-supported interventions during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of individuals employed through project-supported interventions.
data_source: Beneficiary surveys, employer and enterprise records, payroll records, project monitoring data, and evaluation reports.
collection_method: Data are collected through household and beneficiary surveys, project monitoring systems, and administrative records, and verified through field verification where applicable.
means_of_verification: Employment registers, payroll records, enterprise records, beneficiary surveys, project monitoring reports, and field verification reports.
assumptions: Project interventions create sustainable employment, and participating enterprises maintain accurate employment records.
limitations: Employment may fluctuate due to seasonal or market conditions and does not reflect job quality or sustainability.

name: Total number of youths benefiting from empowerment schemes (#)
definition: The total number of young women and men who have experienced measurable benefits from youth empowerment schemes during the reporting period. Benefits may include improved employment, income, entrepreneurship or other livelihood opportunities. Each youth beneficiary is counted once during the reporting period.
numerator: Number of youth beneficiaries.
calculation_method: Count the total number of unique youth beneficiaries who received measurable benefits from project-supported youth empowerment schemes during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of youth benefiting from project-supported youth empowerment schemes.
data_source: Beneficiary registration database, household surveys, training and employment records, project monitoring data, and evaluation reports.
collection_method: Data are collected through household and beneficiary surveys, project monitoring systems, and administrative records, and verified through field verification where applicable.
means_of_verification: Beneficiary databases, household survey reports, training and employment records, project monitoring reports, and field verification reports.
assumptions: Youth actively participate in project interventions, and reliable beneficiary records are maintained.
limitations: Benefits may take time to materialize and may be influenced by external economic or labour market conditions.

name: Total number of women benefiting from women empowerment initiatives (#)
definition: The total number of women who have experienced measurable benefits from women empowerment initiatives during the reporting period. Benefits may include improved income, employment, or other livelihood opportunities. Each beneficiary is counted once during the reporting period.
numerator: Number of women beneficiaries.
calculation_method: Count the total number of women who received measurable benefits from project-supported women empowerment initiatives during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of women benefiting from project-supported women empowerment initiatives.
data_source: Beneficiary registration database, household surveys, training and employment records, project monitoring data, and evaluation reports.
collection_method: Data are collected through household and beneficiary surveys, project monitoring systems, and administrative records, and verified through field verification where applicable.
means_of_verification: Beneficiary databases, household survey reports, training and employment records, project monitoring reports, and field verification reports.
assumptions: Women actively participate in project interventions, and reliable beneficiary records are maintained.
limitations: Empowerment outcomes may take time to materialize and may be influenced by external social, economic, or policy factors.

name: Rice self-sufficiency rate (%)
definition: The percentage of national rice demand met through domestic rice production during the reporting period. The indicator measures the country's progress towards reducing dependence on imported rice and increasing national food security through project-supported interventions.
numerator: Total domestic rice production available for consumption during the reporting period.
denominator: Total national rice demand (or total national rice consumption) during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Calculate the proportion of total national rice consumption supplied by domestic rice production during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of women benefiting from project-supported women empowerment initiatives.
data_source: National agricultural statistics, Ministry of Agriculture reports, customs records, food balance sheets, project reports, and rice sector reports.
collection_method: Compile national production data and national consumption or demand estimates from official government statistics and validated sector reports.
means_of_verification: Ministry of Agriculture reports, National Bureau of Statistics publications, customs/import records, agricultural surveys, and official national reports.
assumptions: Domestic rice production increases, and reliable national production statistics are available.
limitations: Rice self-sufficiency may be influenced by external factors beyond the project's control, including climate, import policies, and market conditions.

name: Percentage increase in rice farmers' average annual income (%)
definition: The percentage increase in the average annual net income earned by project-supported rice farmers during the reporting period compared with the baseline.
numerator: Total domestic rice production available for consumption during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Calculate the average annual net income of project-supported rice farmers, compare it with the baseline average income, and express the change as a percentage.
formula: [(Average annual income during the reporting period − Average annual baseline income) ÷ Average annual baseline income] × 100
data_source: Household surveys, farm records, beneficiary income surveys, cooperative records, project monitoring data, and evaluation reports.
collection_method: Income data are collected through household surveys, beneficiary interviews, and farm records.
means_of_verification: Household survey reports, beneficiary databases, farm records, cooperative records, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Farmers accurately report income, and reliable baseline and follow-up data are available.
limitations: Income may be affected by external factors, and self-reported income may be subject to recall bias.

name: National poverty rate (%)
definition: The percentage of the national population living below the nationally defined poverty line during the reporting period. The indicator measures the project's long-term contribution to reducing poverty through increased agricultural productivity, higher incomes, employment creation, and improved livelihood
numerator: Number of individuals living below the national poverty line.
calculation_method: Determine the proportion of the national population living below the official national poverty line during the reporting period.
formula: (Number of individuals living below the national poverty line ÷ Total national population) × 100
data_source: National household surveys, National Bureau of Statistics, Ministry of Finance reports, census data, and official government publications.
collection_method: Poverty estimates are obtained from nationally representative household surveys and official government statistics.
means_of_verification: National household survey reports, poverty assessment reports, census reports, and official government statistics.
assumptions: Reliable national poverty data are available, and project interventions contribute to improved livelihoods.
limitations: National poverty levels are influenced by external factors beyond the project's control, so attribution should be interpreted with caution.

name: Total number of beneficiaries reached (#)
definition: The total number of individuals who directly benefited from one or more interventions during the reporting period. Beneficiaries may receive support through training, agricultural inputs, irrigation, or other project activities. Each beneficiary is counted once regardless of the number interventions received.
numerator: Number of beneficiaries reached.
calculation_method: Count the total number of individuals who received one or more direct project benefits during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of beneficiaries reached during the reporting period.
data_source: Attendance registers, distribution registers, training records, cooperative records and project monitoring database
collection_method: Data are collected through beneficiary registration systems, attendance sheets, distribution records, training records, and project monitoring tools.
means_of_verification: Attendance registers, distribution registers, training reports, beneficiary surveys and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Beneficiaries are accurately registered, and project records are complete and consistently maintained.
limitations: This indicator measures the number of beneficiaries reached, not the magnitude or quality of benefits received or changes in income, productivity, or well-being.

name: Total number of water harvesting schemes rehabilitated or constructed and made functional (#)
definition: The total number of water harvesting schemes rehabilitated or newly constructed through project support that have been completed, inspected, commissioned, and confirmed to be functional during the reporting period. Each scheme is counted once after it has been officially handed over and confirmed to be operational.
numerator: Number of water harvesting schemes functional during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count each water harvesting scheme functional during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of water harvesting schemes rehabilitated or constructed and made functional during the reporting period.
data_source: Engineering completion reports, inspection reports, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from engineering and contractor reports, and field verification confirming operational status.
means_of_verification: Engineering completion reports, technical inspection reports, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Construction is completed to approved standards, and responsible institutions operate and maintain the schemes.
limitations: This indicator measures functional infrastructure, not its long-term performance, utilization, or benefits to users.

name: Number of Water User Associations (WUAs) and other community groups established (#)
definition: The total number of Water User Associations (WUAs) and other community groups established and made operational through project support during the reporting period. Other community groups may include community-based organizations established to support water resource management, operation and maintenance of infrastructure or other project-related activities. Each group is counted once after verification of its operational status.
numerator: Number of Water User Associations (WUAs) and other community groups established and made operational during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count each Water User Association (WUA) and community group operational.
formula: Total number of Water User Associations (WUAs) and other community groups established and made operational during the reporting period.
data_source: Group registration records, membership registers, project reports, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from implementing partners, membership records, and field visits confirming operational status.
means_of_verification: Registration documents, membership registers, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Communities establish and actively participate in operational groups with adequate project support.
limitations: This indicator measures group establishment, not their effectiveness, or long-term sustainability.

name: Total number of community-based shared solar panel systems with accessories installed (#)
definition: The total number of community-based shared solar panel systems with associated accessories installed, tested, commissioned, and made operational through project support during the reporting period. Each solar system is counted once after successful installation, commissioning, and handover.
numerator: Number of community-based shared solar panel systems installed and operational during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count each community-based shared solar panel system once after installation, and verification as operational during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of community-based shared solar panel systems with accessories installed and made operational during the reporting period.
data_source: Procurement records, installation reports, handover certificates, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from contractors and verified through site inspections, handover certificates, and field visits confirming operational status.
means_of_verification: Procurement records, installation reports, handover certificates, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Solar systems are installed to approved specifications, and communities have the capacity to operate and maintain them.
limitations: This indicator measures installed and operational systems, not utilization, or long-term sustainability.

name: Total number of community-based biogas systems constructed and made operational (#)
definition: The total number of community-based biogas systems constructed and made operational through project support during the reporting period. Each system is counted once after verification.
numerator: Number of community-based biogas systems constructed and made operational during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count each community-based biogas system once after construction, handover, and verification as operational during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of community-based biogas systems constructed and made operational during the reporting period.
data_source: Engineering completion reports, handover certificates, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from contractors and verified through site inspections, handover certificates, and field visits confirming operational status.
means_of_verification: Engineering completion reports, asset registers, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Biogas systems are constructed to approved standards, and communities have the capacity to operate and maintain them.
limitations: This indicator measures operational biogas systems, not their utilization, performance, or long-term sustainability.

name: Total number of submersible pumps with accessories installed in deep boreholes and made operational (#)
definition: The total number of submersible pumps with associated accessories installed in project-supported deep boreholes, tested, commissioned, and made operational during the reporting period. Each pump is counted once after verification.
numerator: Number of submersible pumps with accessories installed in deep boreholes and made operational during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count each submersible pump once after installation, handover, and verification as operational during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of submersible pumps with accessories installed in deep boreholes and made operational during the reporting period.
data_source: Procurement records, installation reports, handover certificates, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from contractors, site inspections, handover documents, and field verification confirming operational status.
means_of_verification: Procurement records, installation reports, commissioning and handover certificates, asset registers, and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Pumps are installed to approved specifications, and communities have the capacity to operate and maintain them.
limitations: This indicator measures operational pumps, not their performance, reliability, or long-term sustainability.

name: Number of cropping cycles adopted
definition: The total number of additional cropping cycles adopted by project beneficiaries during the reporting period as a result of project-supported interventions. Each cropping cycle refers to one complete crop production cycle from planting to harvest.
numerator: Total number of additional cropping cycles adopted by project beneficiaries.
calculation_method: Count additional number of cropping circles adopted through project-supported interventions during the reporting period.
formula: Total number of additional cropping circles adopted during the reporting period.
data_source: Farm production records, extension reports
collection_method: Data is collected through routine field monitoring, farmer production records and from extension reports.
means_of_verification: Farm records, extension reports, crop calendars and project monitoring reports.
responsible: Extension officers, Project Manager and M&E Unit
assumptions: Irrigation infrastructure is functional, farmers have access to production inputs, weather conditions support crop production, and extension services are effectively delivered.
limitations: Weather variability, pest outbreaks, disease incidence, or market constraints may reduce the number of cropping cycles completed.

name: Total number of district floors constructed or rehabilitated (#)
definition: The total number of district floors constructed or rehabilitated during the reporting period. A district floor is considered developed when construction or rehabilitation has been completed, inspected, and officially handed over for use. Each drying floor is counted once upon formal acceptance.
numerator: Total number of district floors constructed or rehabilitated during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Sum the number of district floors constructed or rehabilitated across all sites during the reporting period.
formula: Sum the number of district floors constructed or rehabilitated across all sites during the reporting period.
data_source: Contractor’s completion reports, infrastructure inventory, and the project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from contractor’s records, and project progress reports.
means_of_verification: Contractor certificates, signed handover certificates, site inspection reports, photographs, and infrastructure inventory.
assumptions: Construction or rehabilitation is completed according to approved technical specifications.
limitations: Construction delays and procurement challenges may affect reporting. This indicator measures infrastructure completion and does not assess operational performance after completion.

name: Total number of Cooperative trainings conducted (#)
definition: The total number of training sessions conducted to strengthen the capacity of agricultural cooperatives during the reporting period. Training may cover cooperative governance, leadership, financial management, or other topics identified in the project work plan. Each completed forum is counted once.
numerator: Total number of cooperative training sessions completed across the project site during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count the total number of training sessions completed during the reporting period based on verified meeting records.
formula: Sum the number of cooperative training sessions conducted across project sites during the reporting period.
data_source: Training attendance registers, facilitator reports, and project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from attendance registers, facilitator reports, and post-training reports.
means_of_verification: Training reports, participant lists and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Training sessions are implemented as planned, cooperative members attend, qualified facilitators deliver the training, and training records are accurate.
limitations: This indicator measures the number of cooperative training sessions conducted but does not assess participant attendance

name: Total number of people trained in the FA trainings (#)
definition: The total number of people trained in the FA during the reporting period. Each completed training is counted once.
numerator: Total number of people trained in FA across the project site during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Count the total number of people trained in FA during the reporting period based on verified meeting records.
formula: Sum the number of people trained in FA across project sites during the reporting period.
data_source: Training attendance registers, facilitator reports, and project monitoring database.
collection_method: Data are collected from attendance registers, facilitator reports, and post-training reports.
means_of_verification: Training reports, participant lists and project monitoring reports.
assumptions: Training sessions are implemented as planned, members attend, qualified facilitators deliver the training, and training records are accurate.
limitations: This indicator measures the number of people trained but does not assess participant’s proficiency

name: Total quantity of fertilizer distributed to farmers through project support (MT)
definition: Fertilizer may include organic and inorganic fertilizer supplied to improve soil fertility and agricultural productivity. The quantity is measured in metric tons (MT) and counted once after verified distribution to farmers.
numerator: Total metric tons of fertilizer distributed to farmers during the reporting period.
calculation_method: Sum the total quantity of fertilizer (in metric tonnes) distributed to eligible farmers during the reporting period
formula: Total metric tons of fertilizer distributed to farmers through project support during the reporting period.
data_source: Procurement records, fertilizer distribution registers, and the project monitoring database
collection_method: Data are collected from procurement and distribution records and warehouse records.
means_of_verification: Procurement records, distribution registers, and the project monitoring database.
assumptions: Fertilizer is procured and distributed according to project plans, farmers receive the intended quantities, and distribution records are complete and accurate.
limitations: This indicator measures the quantity of fertilizer distributed to farmers but does not assess whether farmers apply the fertilizer correctly.
